captures.q: Where does “From the Position of the Rejected: Aristotle's Politics Read from Where It Is Written (v1.1)” by Lee Sharks (Alexanarch deposit #1806, AXN:0D5D) lead beyond itself: what does it make it possible to write, read or build next? Ground your answer in the documents.
captures.description: FROM THE POSITION OF THE REJECTED (#1806 v1.1) ON CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT, INCOGNITO, 2026-11-28, AT THE LINK 'LINES OF FLIGHT': three scales (the sentence, the city, the archive); the metic (1275a), the honourless citizen (1278a), the stranger (1324a), the one too great (1284b), the one outside by chance; the Erechtheion accounts (23 citizens, 40 metics, 22 enslaved, 85); Apology 17d with Second Letter 314c; Neleus, Apellicon, Sulla, Tyrannion, Andronicus (Strabo 13.1.54; Plutarch, Sulla 26, Lucullus 19.7); six records it connects (#1785, #1791, #1767, #1800, #1802, #1523); the essay's own open seams listed.

atoms.evidence: Lee Sharks's From the Position of the Rejected
From the Position of the Rejected
The essay does not establish Aristotle's subjective feelings or intentions.
It makes it possible to read institutions, texts and intellectual traditions not from the position of the people they recognize as their authors, citizens or legitimate inheritors
Extends the future-reader sequence through Plato.
Lee Sharks, #1806 — From the Position of the Rejected (v1.1)
Version 1.1 makes a particularly important move from political theory to material history.
